rules.rule: Do not mistake a small set of loose conditions for a constrained strategy.
rules.evidence: V13.4.29 produced 5052 expanded short trades and near-total loss.

rules.rule: Do not rely only on EMA rejection plus MACD/RSI weakening for short research.
rules.evidence: The shortScore design still generated excessive low-quality entries.

rules.rule: A loose shortScore can create overtrading even when each condition looks reasonable alone.
rules.evidence: The 1h strategy averaged hundreds of trades per month across the expanded sample.

rules.rule: Short research must explicitly monitor rebound and squeeze risk.
rules.evidence: The report lacks per-trade regime attribution and stop_loss dominated losses.

rules.rule: Short research must reduce trade frequency or use stronger trigger quality before expansion.
rules.evidence: 5052 trades amplified stop-loss frequency and slippage-adjusted losses.

rules.rule: Regime context cannot be ignored, but it should be evaluated before becoming a hard switch.
rules.evidence: Regime background is available, but V13.4.29 has no per-trade regime attribution.

rules.rule: Do not try to rescue a deeply negative expanded backtest with small parameter tweaks.
Failed research strategies should be archived as benchmark/reference assets, not deleted.
rules.evidence: The failure explains what not to repeat in later short research.

rules.rule: Any future short strategy must include per-trade regime attribution before next-stage review.
rules.evidence: Current report only has background regime distribution, not trade-level attribution.

rules.rule: Any future short strategy must report separated direction metrics, costs, and stop-loss sources.
rules.evidence: V13.4.29 demonstrates that stop_loss and slippage can dominate headline results.

futureRequirements: public funding/OI support before renewed short research
